issues.claim: legal_privacy[7]: "The guidance's own example of deployment-stage harm is the FTC's Rite Aid allegations."
issues.problem: Contradicted. In DCR's Jan 2025 guidance, Rite Aid is used as the example under the 'Training' heading (how biased training data can produce biased outcomes) and cites the FTC complaint. The 'Deployment' example in the same guidance is the now-discontinued PredPol predictive-policing algorithm. Rite Aid is not offered as the deployment-stage example. Everything else in that bullet (LAD covers employment/housing/public accommodation/credit/contracting; liability for a third-party tool the entity did not develop; no new requirements; not enforced as a substitute for the LAD) is confirmed.
issues.fix: Replace with: 'The guidance's training-stage example is the FTC's Rite Aid allegations; its deployment-stage example is PredPol,' or drop the sentence. Keep the Rite Aid citation, but cite the FTC complaint/order rather than the DCR guidance for the false-positive facts.

issues.claim: legal_privacy[2] / gap_for_local_installer: recording inside a private dressing stall is 'prohibited outright' with 'no notice exception'.
issues.problem: Overstated as settled law. N.J.S.A. 2C:14-9(f) makes observing/recording in a private dressing stall a violation of subsection a. or b., but 2C:14-9(d) supplies an affirmative defense to 'a crime under this section' where the actor gave prior notice and acted with a lawful purpose. The safe reading for a client is still 'no cameras in stalls', but 'no notice exception' is an interpretation, not statutory text.
issues.fix: Soften to: '2C:14-9(f) makes it a violation of subsection a./b. to record in a private dressing stall; the general prior-notice affirmative defense in (d) means a lawyer should confirm whether any notice could cure it — the defensible design is no cameras in or aimed into stalls.'

issues.claim: measured_outcomes[5]: "The journal version reports precision/recall of about 82.5%/84.6% but the Wiley page returned HTTP 403 and those two figures are unverified here."
issues.problem: Misleading. The arXiv preprint 2408.00792 itself reports precision 82.46% and recall 84.62% (Table 3, LogReg row, which is also the source of the 83.59% accuracy already cited). Only the journal version is unreadable, not those two figures.
issues.fix: State the 82.46%/84.62% precision/recall as verified from the preprint, and note only that the journal (Wiley) version could not be opened.

issues.claim: buyers[2]: NJ health-care facilities must assess 'non-working surveillance cameras and CCTV "as necessary"' (N.J.A.C. 8:43E-11.7).
issues.problem: Partly unsupported wording. The text I opened requires the annual violence risk assessment to consider 'non-working alarm systems, communication devices, surveillance cameras and/or mirrors' among physical-environment risk factors; it does not say CCTV is assessed 'as necessary', and it does not frame cameras as a control to be assessed. The item is flagged as unverified, which mitigates, but the quoted phrase does not appear.
issues.fix: Reword to what the rule says ('risk assessment must consider non-working surveillance cameras among other physical-environment risk factors') and drop the quote.
